title: Don't Drop the BATON: Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation via Agentic Subtask Exploration and Transition-aware Memory
abstract: arXiv:2608.16889v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Long-horizon robot manipulation chains many contact-rich skills into one multi-stage task. Vision-language-action (VLA) models increasingly master the individual skills, yet the chain still fails: errors compound beyond the policy's ability to correct, and one subtask silently constrains the next. A promising recipe freezes the VLA and puts an LLM agent in charge: it plans in language, moves in free space with analytic primitives, invokes the VLA only for contact-rich segments, and writes adaptation into language memory. Applied to long horizons, it breaks twice. (1) Competence comes from whole-task exploration at test time, whose cost is multiplicative in stages: if one stage needs T episodes, a K-stage task needs about T^K, and a failure does not reveal which stage caused it. translated_title: 不要掉棒：通过智能子任务探索和过渡感知记忆实现长时程机器人操作
translated_abstract: 长时程机器人操作将许多接触丰富的技能串联成一个多阶段任务。视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型越来越擅长掌握单个技能，但整个链条仍然会失败：误差累积超出了策略的纠正能力，一个子任务会无声地限制下一个子任务。一个有前景的解决方案是冻结VLA模型，并由LLM智能体负责：它以语言进行规划，用解析原语在自由空间中移动，仅在接触丰富的片段调用VLA，并将适应性写入语言记忆。应用于长时程任务时，它会在两方面失效。（1）能力来源于测试时的全任务探索，其成本随阶段数呈乘法增长：如果一个阶段需要T次试验，K阶段任务需要约T^K次，而失败不会揭示是哪个阶段导致的。（2）它缺乏对过渡的表示：VLA原语带有退出条件但没有进入条件，因此一个子任务可能以后续子任务无法使用的方式成功。
tldr: 本文针对长时程机器人操作中VLA模型链式任务失败的问题，提出通过智能子任务探索和过渡感知记忆来降低探索成本并确保子任务间的兼容性。
en_tdlr: This paper addresses long-horizon robot manipulation failures in VLA chains by proposing agentic subtask exploration and transition-aware memory to reduce exploration cost and ensure subtask compatibility.
